title: Ottawa knee rule
subtitle: Need for radiography after acute knee injury
summary: Determines whether knee radiography is indicated after acute knee injury.
population: People over 2 years with acute knee injury when fracture is being considered.

criteria.label: Isolated patellar tenderness
criteria.description: Tenderness of the patella with no other bony knee tenderness.

criteria.label: Tenderness at the head of the fibula
Unable to take 4 weight-bearing steps immediately and during assessment
criteria.description: Four steps are required, even if limping.

results.label: No X-ray indicated
interpretation: No knee X-ray indicated by the Ottawa knee rule.

results.label: X-ray indicated
interpretation: Knee X-ray indicated: one or more criteria are present.

overrides: Deformity, open injury, absent or reduced distal pulses, new sensory or motor deficit, locked knee, extensor mechanism failure, or inability to mobilise safely overrides a reassuring score.
limitations: This determines need for fracture imaging only.

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Formal clinical verification has not yet been recorded. Population, exclusions, thresholds, calculations, wording and implementation tests must be checked against the cited source.
